releases.body:
Fix: the published model table now matches the route it describes.

On the VPS the gateway offered `minimax-m3.1-flash-free` a 3,491,182-token window against 1,048,092 the route had served, `deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` 1,233,222 against the 326,000 measured, `big-pickle` a 32,000-token output where the route named 131,072 in a refusal, and `nemotron-3.5-super-vl-free` an 8,192-token output for a model whose 1,000,000-token ask was answered 200.

- An encoded attachment is no longer counted as prompt text: a `data:` URI, or a bare base64 field under a `type`, `mime_type` or `media_type`, is skipped. A 10 MB screenshot became 3,498,676 "tokens" of base64, and that floor was published back as the model's window.
- The estimate scale moves to 3, which drops the brackets measured by the counting that included attachments — those windows were sizes the route was never asked for.
- A completion ceiling the route stated itself (`route` or `route-twin` in the table, or a refusal seen at runtime) now outranks a smaller models.dev claim; a larger claim still wins.
- With no paid twin, models.dev's row for the route id itself and the canonical aggregate are both read and the larger wins (NVIDIA's canonical 8192 vs the route row's 131072; minimax's canonical 524288 vs the row's 512000).
- The discovery cache version moves to 3, so a listing cached with the old limits is fetched again.
- bun test 775 pass; CI green.

Fix: a full review closes transport, discovery, limits and workflow defects.

- provider/stream: upstream hop-by-hop and stale body headers are dropped through one shared helper, so a relayed 403 or 429 can no longer forward the `x-hop` a `Connection` token names; the upstream status is kept instead of collapsing every reply to 200.
- tool-response: an upstream failure is answered with the project's own message, ABORT_ERR counts as an abort rather than a failure, and a rejected body reader is cancelled with the read error.
- models: the discovery cache is versioned (v2), read through a bounded reader instead of an unbounded one, and refetched when another version wrote it.
- limits: the profile is resolved once per sweep run (a config failure used to be retried three times and charged three requests), and --stale-after now requires digits so a date cannot supply a year.
- entries: audit, sweep, watch and capture share the "argv means script, no argv means import" rule, so importing them no longer throws on Node below 22.18.
- capture: every read target comes back through one helper.
- workflows: the gate fails when a scan stage fails (PIPESTATUS, not pipefail alone), concurrent runs are found by the newest updatedAt rather than creation order, and the PR base and compare links keep the default branch.
- bun test 773 pass, and each of the 12 files also passes on its own; CI green on Node 18.17.0 and 24.x; published to npm as 0.5.2.

Fix: models.dev output lookup strips the -free suffix and reads the paid twin.

- 'deepseek-v4.1-flash-free' now reads models.dev's 'deepseek-v4.1-flash' in the opencode provider: output 384000, not 1048576. The 0.5.0 maximum was poisoned by resellers that copy context into limit.output.
- Same for glm-5.3-flash (131072), beam (131072), mimo (131072), minimax (524288), longcat (131072), nemotron lightning (262144), etc.
- With no paid twin, the canonical first-party/most-common output is the fallback; models.dev's direct non-canonical entries (big-pickle 32000) are used when available.
- bun test 735 pass; CI green.

Completion ceilings now follow models.dev's largest claim; only context is measured.

- models.dev is read for both context and output. For every model with a canonical id, the largest limit.output among the entries for that model is the declaration, applied in both directions (it may raise or lower a stale catalogue/table figure).
- The sweep still asks only for sixteen completion tokens and brackets prompts: no output probing. Table/live output tiers remain fallback only for ids models.dev does not describe.
- Tests cover output-only claims, max-not-vote, lowering a stale claim, table/live ignored when models.dev answers, and the no-claim fallback. bun test 731 pass; CI test/node-host/gate green.
- Note: models.dev has no canonical entry for Zen-only ids such as big-pickle; those keep the catalogue/table fallback.

The plugin now reads the limits snapshot the scheduled workflow publishes, so new measurements reach installed hosts without an npm release.

- Default source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tkhs101/OpenCode-Zen-FreeX/main/limits-observed.json (the same limits-observed.json the walls workflow merges into main).
- Startup installs the local cache before the first model list; a background fetch (one per hour, 5 s timeout, single-flight) updates it. No request ever waits on GitHub.
- 256 KiB streamed body cap, version/row/numeric validation (including named windows at the 4M-token ceiling), zero-valid documents never wipe the table; cache writes are atomic and 0600.
- Precedence: explicit file > OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_LIMITS_SNAPSHOT (path or empty) > cache/remote > bundled. OPENCODE_ZEN_FREE_LIMITS_SNAPSHOT_URL/CACHE/REFRESH_MS/TIMEOUT_MS configure the layer.
- One-time upgrade: 0.3.x does not read the remote; after 0.4.0, workflow data needs no release. Unreachable raw GitHub falls back to cache/bundled (documented; mirror URL supported).
- Audit: R7-01..R7-07 findings fixed and independently verified; bun test 729 pass, CI test/node-host/gate green.
